newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolans doubtful over unity government deadline.
newsitem.headline: Angolans doubtful over unity government deadline.

text.p: Negotiators for Angola's leaders and the former rebels with whom they hope to form a new national unity government next weekend said on Monday they were doubtful they could pull it off on time.

"As for an inauguration on January 25, I do not see it happening. I'm sorry, I do not," Isaias Samakuva, the negotiator for the former UNITA rebel movement, told Reuters after talks at a U.N. mediation forum.
Joao Gaspar, a representative for the ruling MPLA government of President Eduardo dos Santos, sounded equally pessimistic despite more upbeat comments from the U.N. mediators themselves.
"I am afraid we just don't have enough time to meet the deadline," he said.
The sticking point in the talks, to try and cement a two-year-old peace which put an end to two decades of civil war, is the role in the government for UNITA leader, Jonas Savimbi.
He declined the offer of a vice-presidency which would have tied him to Luanda, the capital and MPLA stronghold, and kept him away from his base and stronghold, Bailundo.
Now the talks are discussing a special role to be created for him as a "principal presidential adviser with executive powers", U.N. spokesman David Wimhurst said.
He said such a post was suggested in a mediation document that both sides were studying.
"We are involved in intensive diplomatic consultations to try to make this come off," Wimhurst said. "Our aim is to ensure that the timetable is met."
A South African delegation led by Deputy President Thabo Mbeki flew to Luanda on Monday for talks on the peace process, but insisted they were not there in a direct mediating role.

South African officials said Mbeki and Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo met Angola's Prime Minister Franca Van Dunem on Monday morning and were scheduled later in the day to meet UNITA's Samakuva and U.N. envoy Alioune Blondin Beye.

The trip follows a meeting of South African cabinet ministers and Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura in Pretoria on Friday. Earlier this month Savimbi met a delegation led by President Nelson Mandela.
De Moura was on a tour of southern African countries to invite heads of state to attend the planned inauguration.
"De Moura also came to personally invite President Mandela to attend Saturday's inauguration," the official told Reuters.
The South African delegation would urge both parties to push forward with the inauguration despite outstanding disagreement on some matters, he said.
